instructions:
This repository is a testbed for Proxmox VE helper scripts. AGENTS.md and .github/agents/pve-script-creator.agent.md are binding, not advisory: when a diff contradicts them, leave a review comment quoting the rule it breaks instead of only mentioning it in the summary.

The shell engine lives in the separate community-scripts/core repository, which is attached as a pattern repository. ct/ and install/ scripts are not standalone -- they source core's build.func and call its helper functions. Before flagging an undefined function or a missing import, look for it in core; before suggesting hand-written download, version-check or runtime-setup logic, check whether core already provides a helper for it, because AGENTS.md forbids reimplementing those.

vm/ scripts change here first and reach ProxmoxVE only by merge, so never suggest editing ProxmoxVE directly.

files.description: Binding conventions for every script in this repository: required header block, helper functions that must be used instead of hand-rolled logic, the anti-pattern list, var_arm64 rules, and Alpine/multi-OS handling.
Structure and checklist a new or changed app script must satisfy: the CT/install/JSON trio, application requirements, and the pre-merge checklist.
Application requirements a newly added script must meet (1,000+ stars, 6+ months old, actively maintained, official release artifacts).

rules.rule: Never accept hand-written download, extraction, version-check or runtime-setup logic where core already ships a helper (fetch_and_deploy_gh_release, check_for_gh_release, setup_nodejs, setup_uv, setup_java, setup_mongodb, setup_deb822_repo, curl_download, arch_resolve). Reimplementing these is listed as an anti-pattern in AGENTS.md.
Reject Docker-based installations. Applications are installed bare-metal into the container.
A pinned upstream URL that embeds a version or a distribution codename will rot. Flag it and ask for a variant resolved at runtime.
Adding or changing an app script means all three files move together: ct/<app>.sh, install/<app>-install.sh and json/<app>.json. Flag a PR that touches one and not the others.

ct/ and install/ scripts carry no comments besides the header. Flag comments that explain a decision or a workaround; that belongs in the PR description. A single short line where the code would look wrong without it is the exception.

After description, a CT script ends with the standard three lines (Completed Successfully, initialized, access URL) and at most one more. Flag if/else, pct exec or setup instructions there; what the user needs goes into the JSON notes.
